All four addressed.

1. CLI `#variant` now wins transiently. `preferredSelection` checks the CLI memo first, `app.tsx` no longer calls `variant.set`, so `model.json` is never overwritten by a flag. `recent` history still updates. Added `CLI variant wins transiently over stored preference without persisting` covering stored-`low` + CLI-`high` → selects `high`, file stays `low`, then in-session switch to `low` sticks.
2. Removed both imperative `set` calls from `onMount`. CLI flows through a `cliModel` memo validated against the loaded catalog, with a recents-only effect after `models()` + `preferences.ready`. No timing dependency. Explicit `selectModel\
/`variant.set` sets `cliSuperseded` so later user switches beat the launch flag.
3. `util/model.ts` delegates to `Model.Ref.parse` with empty-on-invalid fallback, preserving the non-string crash guard. Strict rules now apply: trailing `#` and multi-`#` are invalid. Tests updated.

Minor: `preferredSelection` takes `ModelSelection`.

Verified: target files 20 pass, `tui typecheck` clean, `oxlint` clean.

Confirmed both shapes on my head before fixing: the split late call came back as `input:{}` on OpenAI Chat, and the late Mistral call came back as `toolCalls: []`.

Fixed per your suggestion:

- OpenAI Chat restores the first-terminal-only gate on the per-frame `finishAll` (openai-chat.ts:1082). Late deltas accumulate in `tools` only; nothing finalizes mid-stream.
- Late tools finalize once in `finishEvents` when the finish is not `length`/`content-filter` (openai-chat.ts:1118), accumulating `[...state.toolCallEvents, ...late.events]`. The filtered-drop test still passes unchanged.
- Mistral gets the same end-of-stream finalization in its `finishEvents` (mistral-chat.ts:709) into `completedTools`, so late calls finalize on both protocols. No per-frame change on Mistral, avoiding the same split bug.
- Accumulation instead of replacement stays, since a late frame can now only finalize once at the end.

On the minor: yes, intentional. Text and reasoning after `length`/`content-filter` are additive output worth keeping; tool calls need confirmation, so they stay dropped for incomplete finishes.

Tests (+3): OpenAI split-args late call finishes with `{city:"Paris"}`; Mistral late complete call finalizes; Mistral split-args late call finishes with full arguments. Verified: target suites 43 pass, full ai suite 1394 pass / 28 skip / 0 fail, ai typecheck clean, lint clean.

checked the docs and this is the regression branch, not the fix branch. Microsoft documents `prompt_cache_key` as supported on Azure OpenAI Chat Completions with no minimum API version (their own example sends it in the Chat body), and OpenAI documents it as a standard top-level routing parameter. So dropping it for Azure would silently lose cache affinity for those users.

Fixed: added `azure` + `openai.azure.com` to the allowlist in `detectSupportsPromptCacheKey`, restoring pre-PR behavior for Azure (which always sent the key). This also matches upstream `27aaa9ce0e`, which sets `supportsPromptCacheKey: true` on the Azure chat route. For non-Azure hosts on a custom domain the compatibility flag remains the opt-in.

Tests: added `sends prompt cache key for Azure Chat endpoints` (resourceName → `.openai.azure.com`, asserts the key is present). Verified: 73/73 in openai-chat.test.ts, 1391 pass full ai suite, typecheck + lint clean.

On the minor: agreed, leaving as-is provider matching is already case-normalized, and custom IDs are covered by baseURL matching plus the compatibility flag.

Same symptom from a different setup — Windows client over SSH, with tmux in between.

### Environment
- **OpenCode:** 1.18.31, running on a headless Ubuntu dev box (not the local machine), spawned under tmux (`TERM=tmux-256color`, no `SSH_TTY` on the opencode process)
- **Client:** Windows 11, connecting to the box via SSH
- **Repro:** select a code block/command in the TUI, press the copy key → toast `Copied to clipboard` appears → paste (Ctrl+V) anywhere on Windows gives the **previous** clipboard content, the new text never arrives.

### Notes / requests
- With three hops (opencode → tmux → SSH → Windows terminal), the OSC52 write needs support at every hop (tmux `set-clipboard on` + `allow-passthrough`, terminal OSC52 enabled). When any hop drops it, opencode still reports success.
- The bad part is the **false success toast**: the user believes it's copied and pastes the wrong thing (in our case: an old PowerShell command into an admin shell). Even without a reliable fallback, detecting that the clipboard didn't change (or that OSC52 is unsupported) and showing a warning instead of `Copied to clipboard` would prevent silent wrong pastes.

Same root cause as #37444, and I hit it **without any model switch**: plain restart + resume (`opencode --continue`) of a long `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` session (Console/Zen path, `xhigh`) reproduces the identical 400 immediately — the first resumed turn fails and every retry in that session fails. The stored reasoning parts carry caller-bound continuation state minted by the *previous* opencode process; replayed into a fresh caller connection, the gateway rejects them. That's #48319's restart trigger, same family, just our error message instead of `rs_A:rs_B not found`.

DB evidence (stock `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, pre-cleanup snapshot):

- `part.data` reasoning rows look like:
  `{"type":"reasoning","text":"<summary>","metadata":{"openai":{"itemId":"rs_…","reasoningEncryptedContent":"Q-Pa…"}}}`
- 233 parts across 7 sessions carried those two fields.
- `message.data` error rows: `APIError · 400 · "reasoning \`encrypted_content\` was not issued to this caller"` from gateway `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/responses`.

Workaround that works today (no upstream change): delete `metadata.openai.itemId` and `metadata.openai.reasoningEncryptedContent` from stored reasoning parts. The visible reasoning summary/text is preserved, and resumed sessions continue cleanly after restart. I made it durable by installing persistent AFTER INSERT/UPDATE triggers on the `part` table so the fields never get persisted again — re-runnable stdlib script, idempotent, re-run after any opencode upgrade that rebuilds the store.

On the proper fix: agree with #37444's patch direction — the request-normalization layer should treat `itemId`/`reasoningEncryptedContent` as **non-durable continuation state**: replay it only for the current in-flight turn (same connection, tool-loop continuation), and keep only the visible summary for historical reasoning when reconstructing input across fork/resume/restart boundaries. The auto-retry fallback in #31236 (on this specific 400, resend once with stale reasoning references dropped) would make all these triggers transparent for every provider.

One more signal worth triaging separately: #49188 (filed today) reports this now happens in **fresh short sessions after 2–3 messages, no resume/compact involved** — suggests the Console gateway started enforcing stricter validation/expiry on the replayed `encrypted_content`. If the normalization fix lands and that repro persists, it points at the gateway side.

Confirmed still present on **v1.18.30** and **v1.18.31** (`v1.18.31` changelog is ACP/TUI/Copilot only; `OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX` is unchanged).

```ts
// packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts
export const OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX = 32_000

export function maxOutputTokens(model: Provider.Model, outputTokenMax = OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX): number {
  return Math.min(model.limit.output, outputTokenMax) || outputTokenMax
}
```

`session/llm/request.ts` then sends that as `maxOutputTokens`. Anthropic budget variants are also clamped with `OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX - 1`.

### What we see

Same silent 32k request cap on reasoning-heavy turns, including models whose catalog already advertises far more:

| Model | Advertised `limit.output` | What OpenCode actually requests |
|---|---:|---:|
| `anthropic/claude-fable-5-1` (Max) | 128000 | 32000 |
| `anthropic/claude-opus-5` | 128000 | 32000 |
| `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` | 128000 | 32000 |
| DeepSeek V4-class via `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` | 64k–384k | 32000 |

On Fable 5.1 Max and DeepSeek thinking, a step can finish `reason: "length"` with reasoning consuming the entire 32k budget and little or no answer/tool call. Title/summary agents that set a small explicit cap are fine; the bug is the global clamp on ordinary/thinking turns.

`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX` still works as a shotgun, but it is global and does not honor per-model `limit.output`.

Please use configured `limit.output` (and any smaller explicit request cap) instead of `Math.min(limit.output, 32000)` for every model.

Cross-checking the §4 point above against `v2`, since it changes what is left to fix here.

**The landmine is real on v2 today.** In `packages/ai/src/provider-error.ts`, the code-phrasing clause
`codes.some((code) => SERVER_CODES.has(code) || code.includes("exhausted") || code.includes("unavailable"))`
is not guarded by HTTP status, so a reworded `quota_exceeded` (e.g. "quota exhausted") would make the
Copilot rejection look retryable. What limits the damage today is the classifier not matching the
current wording plus the bounded schedule — `packages/core/src/session/runner/retry.ts` returns `false`
for `QuotaExceeded` and caps retries at `Schedule.recurs(4)`.

**That classification fix is already in flight upstream, so it does not need a PR from here.**
Maintainer PR #49195 (`fix(ai): classify gateway account limits as quota and keep 4xx non-retryable`)
does exactly what §4 asks for: it adds `input.status === 402` to the quota branch — which makes the
captured `402 quota_exceeded` terminal regardless of wording or whether the code is listed — and moves
the server-code / `exhausted` / `unavailable` matching under the existing `status === undefined || status < 400`
guard, so server phrasing can no longer override a 4xx rejection. If you were considering a PR for the
retry side, that one supersedes it.

What remains for this issue is therefore the request-amplification side that the report actually
measures: how many Copilot calls a single prompt issues. A legacy per-request plan is charged per call,
so the fixes outlined earlier still stand — the `x-initiator` / interaction-type handling for non-agent
calls, and routing opencode2's small-model work back to a Copilot-supported small model instead of
spending full-size requests on it. I still hold this issue for that part; status is unchanged from
comment 5638928451.

- Large user base in emerging markets still on armv7 devices; they can't run the current arm64/amd64 releases

**Suggested approach:**
- Add `linux/arm/v7` to release matrix (goreleaser `goarch: [amd64, arm64, arm]` + docker `platforms: linux/arm/v7`)
- Document manual build: `GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=7 go build ./...` / `bun build --target=bun-linux-arm` where applicable

Hit this too, worth noting a variant symptom: it also causes a **crash loop on every `opencode` startup**, not just during a live session.

My case: a session had a PDF (`AI_Engineering.pdf`) attached twice, each ingested as a ~308 MB `data:application/pdf;base64,...` string. `opencode.log` showed this on *every single launch*:

```
message="schema rejection" kind=Body reason="RangeError: Out of memory"
```

i.e. schema validation of the session/message body OOMs before the TUI even becomes usable — so once a session gets into this state, every subsequent startup fails, not just the one where the PDF was ingested.

`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` had ballooned to **1.4 GB** (two ~308 MB rows in `part`, matching the pattern in the issue description). Deleting that one session's rows (`part`, `message`, `event`, `event_sequence`, `session`) and running `VACUUM` brought it down to **226 MB**, and startup stopped OOMing.

Given the root cause described above, it'd also be good if the startup-time schema/body validation failed gracefully per-session (e.g. skip/quarantine the offending session) rather than OOMing the whole process — right now a single bad session can permanently break `opencode` from launching at all until someone manually edits the SQLite DB.
